name: Market Intelligence
summary: A local-first research workspace that turns market observations into testable hypotheses.
why: Keeps the chain from market context to company evidence and a falsifiable hypothesis visible.
technical: A local DuckDB warehouse retains dated observations and ingestion provenance. The browser reads exported snapshots and provides transparent screens, versioned hypothesis logs, and local portfolio inputs.
demonstrates: Data provenance, explainable decision support, and an architecture that separates research from execution.
boundary: Research-only historical snapshots. No broker or trade execution; option chains, implied volatility, and option mark-to-market are not connected.

name: Referral
summary: Evidence-led career intelligence with fit scores you can inspect and next steps you can act on.
why: Connects career goals, evidence, and opportunities in one repeatable decision loop.
technical: Deterministic scoring exposes its component breakdown, matched evidence, and gaps. Isolated industry workspaces persist in browser storage.
demonstrates: Explainability, configurable workflows, and useful decision support before introducing model complexity.
boundary: Synthetic profiles and opportunities. Login, billing, live research sources, and external AI drafting are not connected.

name: Powderline
summary: A source-aware mountain camera wall for a clearer read before heading into Colorado’s high country.
why: Reduces the friction of checking resort cameras and finding the official conditions source.
technical: A curated camera catalog handles provider differences, on-demand video, resort filtering, and refresh failures while retaining the last successful image.
demonstrates: External-source orchestration, resilient interface states, and careful boundaries around incomplete operational data.
boundary: Camera availability depends on providers. Resort report adapters, live road conditions, accounts, and alerts are not connected.

name: EasyEcom
summary: A configurable storefront engine, explored through a Colorado-inspired Après Club concept brand.
why: Makes the catalog, product decisions, and bag feel like one coherent shopping experience.
technical: Typed brand configuration separates catalog and identity from commerce components. Variant validation and integer pricing keep the demonstration bag consistent.
demonstrates: Reusable product architecture, interaction design, and explicit boundaries between a storefront demo and commerce operations.
boundary: Concept artwork and illustrative catalog. Captured in POC mode with simulated checkout and payments disabled.

name: SimpleSLP
summary: A clinical workflow prototype connecting cases, goals, interventions, and recorded progress.
why: Keeps the evidence behind the next care decision connected to the work that produced it.
technical: A relational case-to-outcome model supports auditable records and draft-to-approval document workflows. AI drafts default to a deterministic offline provider.
demonstrates: Traceable workflows, human review of generated drafts, and privacy-aware local system design.
boundary: Fresh synthetic patient records only. Mock AI is the default; this prototype is not validated for clinical use.
